description: State of one quote, as the promotion engine sees it. Not the internal state of any participant.

requested.description: A cart has arrived; the latency budget starts counting here.

CART_ACCEPTED.description: Currency and subtotal are readable, so candidates can be selected.

evaluating.description: Candidates are being filtered and priced inside the budget.

BUDGET_EXCEEDED.description: Whatever was computed is discarded — a half-priced cart is worse than none.

scanning-promotions.description: Looping automatic promos: window, segment, minimum spend, campaign budget.

validating-coupon.description: Asking coupon-service whether the presented code may still be used.

COUPON_REFUSED.description: A refused code is a rejection line, never a failed request.

quoted.description: A complete quote exists and is readable until it expires.

COUPON_PRESENTED.description: A later code re-opens the evaluation against the same cart.

COUPON_WITHDRAWN.description: The customer removed a code. Re-evaluated from scratch, because an automatic promo may have lost to it.

QUOTE_SUPERSEDED.description: A re-quote produced a newer quote for the same cart. This one is closed without ever having been wrong.

degraded.description: Answered without a full evaluation; fallback is set and applied is empty.

ORDER_PLACED.description: The order is placed undiscounted. No redemption is published.

QUOTE_SUPERSEDED.description: The usual escape from a degraded quote: the engine recovered and a re-quote answered properly.

committed.description: The cart became an order at the quoted price; any coupon is now burnt.

expired.description: Nobody converted the cart in time. Nothing was spent and nothing is owed.

superseded.description: Replaced by a newer quote for the same cart. Distinct from expired: the customer is still shopping, and the basket must not say the offer lapsed.

refused.description: The request itself was wrong — the only outcome that is a problem document.
